text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines expected to announce drastic economy measures with Q3 results on Tuesday. (p1)
- Shares in television production group Endemol soar from 48 guilders to 56.50 on first day of trading. (p1)
- Publisher VNU takes 50 pct stake in TV production firm IDTV. (p1)
- Analysts' profit forecasts for the 25 companies in the AEX index were reviseddown in October from September. (p1)
- Kitchen appliance, heating equipment and bicycle firm Atag Q3 net drops to 1.3 million guilders from 4.5 million; company expects 30-40 pct lower full year profit. (p3)
- Port and trading company Furness expects to return to profitability this year. (p3)
- Wholesale pharmaceutical cooperative OPG seeks rapid expansion in Belgium. (p4)
- Small and mid-sized businesses organisation MKB says costs of processing smart-card payments are too high. (p4) DE VOLKSKRANT
- 30 civil servants responsible for welfare benefits in Amsterdam commit fraud, according to investigation. (p1)
- Unions expect KLM spending cuts to hit management jobs. (p2)
- ABN AMRO Bank seeks to strengthen its position in Japanese capital markets. (p2)
- Coalition party D66 wants reduction in traffic at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, with some flights transferred to other airports. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Environment minister Margaretha de Boer in favour of 90 km speed limit on motorways. (p1)
- Utility companies PNEM of North Brabant and Mega of Limburg to merge. (p13)
TROUW
- Charter companies Transavia and Martinair cancel planned investments in Maastricht Airport after cabinet's restriction on night flights. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Prime Minister Wim Kok annoyed at opposition of coalition parties Labour and D66 to planned High Speed Rail-line. (p1)
- Oil group Royal Dutch/Shell sets up Internet site to enter into dialogue with the public. (p11)
